subheader.text: The Panama Canal

subpoints.text: The Panama Canal is a waterway that cuts through the middle of Panama to connect the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. It is one of the most important shipping routes in the world. Before it opened in 1914, ships had to travel all the way around the tip of South America to get from one ocean to the other!

The 48-mile-long, man-made canal was one of the biggest and most difficult engineering projects in history. France started work in 1881, and the United States took over in 1904. The United States fully controlled the canal and the land around it from the time it opened in 1914 until 1978. Today, Panama owns and controls the canal.

subheader.text: Why does the Dominican Republic share its island with another country?

pieces.text: The Dominican Republic and Haiti share the island of
. It is home to the earliest European settlements in the Americas. Christopher Columbus founded the first European settlement on the island in 1492 during his first voyage across the Atlantic.

subpoints.text: Though many people lived on the island before Columbus's arrival, European countries quickly began to colonize the island. Eventually France and Spain both established colonies. The Spanish colony eventually became the country of the Dominican Republic, and the French colony eventually became the country of Haiti. Today, people in the two countries speak different languages and have many cultural differences.

subheader.text: Does Cuba have any territorial disputes?

pieces.text: . In other words, multiple countries or groups claim that the area rightfully belongs to them.

subpoints.text: The United States controls the area and uses it as a military base and prison. A treaty in 1903 gave the U.S. the right to rent the land from Cuba. But today, Cuba says that it had no choice but to accept the treaty. It wants the United States to leave the area and does not accept the rent money sent by the United States each year.
